ratings.note: f1: only skippers who need to change the date, though the most-reported issue (15/100); i3: session participants searched 38-75 s, some restarted or said they would phone (support contact); p1: once found under the three dots it is known, but use is a few times a season. s=4; rated 3 because restarting from the short first page is a working, if costly, recovery.

f1: only when length exceeds the chosen berth (11/100, fed by the LOA and unit ambiguities); i3: screenshot shows a dead end with only a code, observed abandonment, retyping and phone calls; p2: the page never says why, so users cannot learn to avoid it. s=4.

f1: boats with a bowsprit, davits or other overhang (6/100); i3: screenshot confirms bare 'Length' label, wrong berth booked and office contact reported; p0: once a skipper learns the limit is LOA they enter it next time. s=3.
f1: skippers who think in feet (4/100); i3: probe 8 shows any positive length accepted, a 34 ft boat got an 8 m berth and the office had to correct it; p0: learned after one correction. s=3.

f2: 10/100 reports and several session participants stopped; small and chartered boats are a common visitor type; i3: required field with no hint blocks the booking for boats without DSC, users phoned; p2: a boat without an MMSI can never get past it. s=4.

f2: every summer-time arrival (8/100 reports); i2: screenshot shows UTC only in the caption next to local arrival times, users arrived an hour off and waited at a closed gate; p1: learned once noticed. s=3.

f2: most listed times fall outside the gate window on any day (7/100 reports); i2: the booking accepts an arrival the boat cannot make, found out at the shut gate; p1: skippers who learn the gate plan around it themselves. s=3.

f3: every berth comparison (screenshot shows only per-metre rates); i1: extra effort, a participant used a calculator for about 45 s; p2: recurs every booking. s=3; rated 2 because the total does appear on review before committing, so no wrong payment results, only effort.
f2: every first-time visitor sees berth/pontoon space/mooring across pages (5/100); i1: hesitation and doubt about price, no failure observed; p0: mostly a first-visit confusion. s=2.

f3: every booking page lacks a step indicator (7/100); i1: uncertainty, no observed failure or abandonment; p1: returning users know the flow length. s=3; rated 2 because the flow is short and no behavioural harm was observed, only self-reported unease.

f2: every first-time visitor (screenshot shows reference, date, berth, nights only); i3: phone calls and one 40-minute wait outside reported; p0: returning skippers already know the channel and gate. s=4; rated 3 because the office number is on the page and VHF channels and gate times are also in pilot books skippers normally carry.
